topic: The six Git commands a first-year uses on every project (clone, status, add, commit, push, pull), with clear commit messages and a cheat sheet
save_reason: A one-slide cheat sheet of the six Git commands with what each does (slide 7, and the full list with examples in the caption).
send_reason: Send this to a friend starting their first coding project.

cover.concept: Cinematic night photo: a quiet student desk in a dark room, lit only by the glow of an open laptop seen from behind, beside it an open notebook with a hand-drawn branching diagram of lines and dots.
hooks: Learn the six Git commands you'll use daily. (confidence)
Use Git the way real project teams do. (ambition)
Git can undo almost any coding mistake. (awe)
Most projects run on just six Git commands. (curiosity)
cover.hookDraft: Learn the six Git commands you'll use daily.

slides.label: Before you add
slides.idea: Re-hook: check git status first; it shows what changed.

slides.line: It shows what changed before you add anything.
slides.screen: A terminal cropped big: `git status` output with 'Changes not staged for commit' and two modified files, one highlighted (.focus)

slides.label: Before you commit
slides.idea: Won't work unless your commit messages say what changed.
slides.title: This won't work unless your messages are clear.
slides.line: Write what changed, like 'Add login form'.

The desk sits in the lower 60% of the frame; the top 35% is calm, dark, empty wall. Portrait 2:3, natural colours, no green tint. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no faces, no watermark.
